clue.text: Spitting Image of Queen, one in oddly accurate representation

indicators.note: in places the Queen-and-one pair inside the jumbled letters
oddly says the letters of the following word are arranged in a strange new way
a representation of a word recasts it, here backing up oddly as a second signal that the word accurate is rearranged

parts.note: R, for Regina, is the standard abbreviation for a queen
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: The satirical puppet show's portrayal of the monarch is strangely true to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly ... representation' jumbles ACCURATE, and 'in' puts R and I inside it. Spitting Image was a British TV satire using grotesque puppets of public figures, the Queen among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitting Image was a British television show built entirely on puppet caricatures, so it stands as an example of one.

clue.text: Get round sort of cable

definitions.meaning: to persuade someone gently, win them over
short for coaxial, a type of cable used for aerials

explanation.surface: Get round sort of cable
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to wheedle someone round, and coax is also short for coaxial cable.

clue.text: Cut grass going over short pipe

indicators.note: going over means the grass word sits around the short pipe

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: short says the word for pipe loses its last letter

parts.note: a duct is a pipe or channel

explanation.surface: Mowing lawn over a stubby drainpipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the pipe word, and 'going over' means the grass word is written around what is left. 'Cut' looks like a verb but is the past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: Reduced means cut back or lowered, as prices are cut, a synonym in the past participle.

clue.text: Puma, an old killer, grabbing at a horse

indicators.note: grabbing means the killer holds the other pieces inside himself

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in the Book of Genesis
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A big cat, once a predator, seizes a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' is a link here. 'old killer' tempts CAT; it is Cain, the first murderer in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Catamountain is an old word for a wild cat such as a puma or leopard.

clue.text: Saving plants from cliffs by sea

definitions.meaning: sea pinks, which grow on coastal cliffs

explanation.surface: Rescuing flowers on the clifftops beside the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift is careful saving of money and also the sea pink, a plant of coastal cliffs.

clue.text: Preliminary version of film score used at end of Rocky

indicators.note: used at end of puts the score word after the word for rocky

parts.note: rocky ground is rough
to score is to cut a line into

explanation.surface: Music for a movie is played as the boxing film Rocky closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like the film title but simply means rough.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough cut is the first assembled edit of a film before final trimming.

clue.text: Smear name with cutting article

indicators.note: cutting means the article slices into the middle of the word for name

parts.note: to dub someone is to name them
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece libels someone by name.
explanation.definitionFit: To daub is to smear paint or mud roughly on a surface, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Doggerel bishop dismissed as harmful

indicators.note: dismissed means the bishop is sent out of the phrase

parts.note: doggerel is bad verse
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman's poor poetry is thrown out as damaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means unfavourable or harmful, as in adverse effects.

clue.text: Where funds were kept in comparatively poor town in novel

indicators.note: in places the money box inside the comparative word

parts.note: barer means more bare, more poorly provided
a chest is a strongbox for money

explanation.surface: Money was stored in a rather impoverished fictional town.
explanation.walkthrough: Barchester is the cathedral town of Trollope's Barchester novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Barchester is the fictional cathedral town of Anthony Trollope's novels, such as Barchester Towers.

clue.text: Review that's old I spotted in funny place for concertgoers

parts.note: an audit is a formal review of accounts

indicators.note: 'in' puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or funny

explanation.surface: Someone checking an old record notices themself in an odd venue full of music lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' and 'spotted in' are only joining words; the pieces simply run in order. RUM meaning strange is British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditorium is the hall where an audience, such as a concert crowd, sits.

clue.text: State of mad speaker losing head

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the word for a mad speaker is dropped

parts.note: a raver is someone who raves, talking wildly as if mad

explanation.surface: A ranting orator ends up decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun (a condition) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state or assert something firmly, a synonym.

clue.text: Study composer, not his son, a!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Study composer, not his son, a!' is cut short: DELIBE(S) gives DELIBE but nothing in 'a!' gives RATION, and 11-down is not on the scan.
annotationWithheld.clue: Study composer, not his son, a!

clue.text: Face home truths after review is rubbish

indicators.note: after review the letters of the phrase are re-examined and set in a new order

explanation.surface: Being made to confront harsh realities after an appraisal is awful.
explanation.definitionFit: The scum of the earth are the most worthless people, rubbish in the slang sense of contemptible.

clue.text: Illicit affairs featured in dirty rhymes

definitions.text: Illicit affairs featured in dirty rhymes

parts.words: Illicit affairs featured in dirty rhymes
parts.note: a reduplicated rhyming phrase for secret naughty behaviour, the sort of thing found in saucy verses

explanation.surface: Bawdy limericks about secret lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanky-panky means illicit sexual goings-on, and its two halves rhyme with each other.

clue.text: Retreating soldiers facing unfriendly fire

indicators.note: retreating means the soldiers go backwards, so their letters are read in reverse

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment
dour means stern and unfriendly

explanation.surface: Troops pull back in the face of hostile shelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreating' turns RA into AR; 'facing' only joins it to DOUR. 'fire' is passion, not gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is fiery passion or enthusiasm, so fire in the emotional sense is a synonym.

clue.text: Baby outfit

definitions.meaning: as in 'that's your baby', one's own concern or responsibility
an outfit is a firm or company

explanation.definitionFit: Business means both one's own particular concern, as a pet project is one's baby, and a commercial firm or outfit.

clue.text: Open area used by guys getting fit

parts.note: guys are men
able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: Public parkland used by men doing exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' and 'getting' are joining words. 'Open' means receptive, not unenclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable means open to persuasion or suggestion, a synonym.

clue.text: Living life — as rhythm section in jazz band must do

definitions.text: as rhythm section in jazz band must do

parts.note: your keep is your living or maintenance, as in earning your keep
life is a prison sentence, doing time

explanation.surface: A jazz musician's life depends on holding the beat steady.
explanation.walkthrough: TIME for 'life' comes from prison slang: a life sentence is doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep time is to hold a steady beat, which is the drummer's and bassist's whole job.

clue.text: Run with wretched mobile ringing and catch up

indicators.note: ringing means the jumbled word encircles the letter for run
wretched means in a bad state, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A jogger with a broken mobile phone goes off and tries to catch up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wretched' turns MOBILE into EMBOIL, and 'ringing' places R inside. 'ringing' suggests a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil is to catch someone up or involve them in a conflict.

clue.text: Soil found in gorge

definitions.meaning: to soil something is to dirty or pollute it
a narrow pass or ravine between hills

explanation.surface: Dirt turns up at the bottom of a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: Defile as a verb means to make dirty, and as a noun a narrow valley that troops file through.

clue.text: Local sight, for example, said to cause anger

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: a local is a British pub, an inn; sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood view is claimed to infuriate people.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'local' is the nearby pub. INN SENSE, spoken, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense is to make someone very angry, so it means to cause anger.

clue.text: Punch wearing his or woman's head coverings

indicators.note: wearing means the word his has the punch inside it, as clothing holds a body

parts.note: a jab is a quick punch

explanation.surface: A blow lands on whichever head scarves belong to him or her.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone getting punched; 'wearing' is the container signal and 'or' is only a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hijabs are the headscarves worn by many Muslim women.

clue.text: General suspicion going round is "I may be a very annoying person"

definitions.text: "I may be a very annoying person"

parts.note: public means general, belonging to everyone

indicators.note: going round says the word for suspicion encircles the little word is

parts.note: a suspicion can mean a faint trace or hint, a nuance

explanation.surface: A widespread rumour circulates that someone is a dreadful pest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a first-person riddle: something describing itself as a source of annoyance. 'suspicion' is used in its sense of a slight trace.
explanation.definitionFit: A public nuisance is an offence or an irritating person, so this one could fairly describe itself as very annoying.

clue.text: Good word for stop up

definitions.meaning: a favourable mention, a puff for a product

explanation.surface: Good word for stop up
explanation.definitionFit: A plug is a promotional good word, and to plug a hole is to stop it up.

clue.text: Number over twelve

parts.note: on can mean over or on top of

explanation.surface: A count that goes past a dozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twelve' is the clock time, midday, not a count.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is twelve o'clock midday, so twelve here names the hour.

clue.text: Like offering island in rigged ballot?

indicators.note: a rigged vote is fixed or tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Iona is a small island in the Scottish Hebrides

explanation.surface: Is it a gift to place an island's vote in a fixed election?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only joins IONA to BALLOT; 'rigged' jumbles the whole pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblational means relating to an oblation, a religious offering, so it describes something like an offering.

clue.text: University bringing back race right away

indicators.note: bringing back means the shortened word is turned round to read backwards
right away says the letter for right is removed

parts.note: a relay is a team race

explanation.surface: A college reinstates a race without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' takes R from RELAY to leave ELAY, which 'bringing back' turns round. The surface reading of 'right away' as 'immediately' misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is a well-known Ivy League university in Connecticut.

clue.text: Nobel prize-winner's novel begins here

indicators.note: novel means new, so the following letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A laureate's book opens at this point.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link. Werner Heisenberg won the 1932 Nobel Prize in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Werner Heisenberg, the physicist of the uncertainty principle, is an example of a Nobel laureate.
